1. (Currently amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a destination, the method comprising:
a. providing a finger palette including:
i. a ring portion that is securable to a finger; and
ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion being at least substantially smooth to allow a user to spread or blend cosmetic product on the surface portion;
b. securing the finger palette to a finger;
c. depositing a cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette __by removing the cosmetic product from the container using an applicator tool before depositing__; and
d. transferring the cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to a destination __using a separate transfer tool__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. a first quantity of the cosmetic product is deposited onto the surface portion; and
b. a second quantity of the cosmetic product is transferred from the surface portion to the destination, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity, __wherein the first quantity and second quantity are measured quantities applied by the user__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. the surface portion extends outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter; and
b. the surface portion is __configured to be__ free, from any first point on the outer perimeter to any second point on the outer perimeter, of features that could trap cosmetics and complicate cleaning of the surface portion, __such that the surface portion is uninterrupted from the surface center to the outer perimeter__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion is at least substantially without protrusions extending therefrom __and is configured to allow an applicator to scrape across the surface portion in an uninterrupted motion__.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the surface portion is at least substantially planar __and extends continuously from a central region to an outer edge without interruption__.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the finger palette is secured to the finger by passing the finger through the ring portion __such that the ring portion is removably and replaceably securable__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 further including the step of removing the cosmetic product from a container before depositing the cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette, __wherein the removing step is performed using a first applicator tool separate from a second transfer tool used to transfer the cosmetic product to the destination__.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein:
a. the cosmetic product is a first cosmetic product; and
b. the method further includes the step of depositing a second cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette __on a non-overlapping segment of the surface portion__.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12 wherein:
a. the first cosmetic product is deposited on a first segment of the surface portion; and
b. the second cosmetic product is deposited on a non-overlapping second segment of the surface portion, __such that the first and second cosmetic products remain visibly distinct on the surface portion__.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12 further including the step of blending the first cosmetic product with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product __using an applicator tool to mix the products together__.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 14 further including the step of transferring the blended cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette to the destination __using a separate transfer tool__.

18. (Currently amended) A method of using a finger palette to transfer cosmetics from a container to a work surface, the method comprising:
a. providing a finger palette including:
i. a ring portion configured to be removably and replaceably securable to a finger; and
ii. a surface portion secured to the ring portion, the surface portion extending outwardly from a surface center to an outer perimeter, wherein the surface portion is at least substantially smooth and __uninterrupted from the surface center to the outer perimeter__ so as to allow a user to scrape an applicator past the surface center in an uninterrupted motion while spreading or blending cosmetic product over the entirety of the surface portion;
b. securing the finger palette to a finger by passing the finger through the ring portion;
c. dispensing cosmetic product from a cosmetics container using a first applicator tool and placing a first quantity of the dispensed cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette;
d. removing cosmetic product from the surface portion of the finger palette __using a second applicator tool separate from the first applicator tool__; and
e. applying a second quantity of the removed cosmetic product to a destination, the second quantity being smaller than the first quantity.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 18 wherein:
a. the dispensed cosmetic product is a first cosmetic product dispensed from a first cosmetics container;
b. the method further includes the steps of:
i. dispensing a second cosmetic product from a second cosmetics container using a second applicator tool and placing a third quantity of the dispensed second cosmetic product onto the surface portion of the finger palette __on a non-overlapping segment of the surface portion__; and
ii. blending the first cosmetic product on the surface portion with the second cosmetic product on the surface portion to obtain a blended cosmetic product, wherein the cosmetic product applied to the destination is the blended cosmetic product __using a third applicator tool__.
